USD.catalyst: The U.S. dollar index sits firmly elevated near 101.03, trading above its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day simple moving averages as it outperforms G10 peers with a +1.04% weekly gain. Resilient Treasury yields and hawkish Federal Reserve rhetoric continue to anchor broad dollar demand, reinforced by Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack warning that an entrenched inflation mindset represents the preeminent risk facing policymakers. Concurrently, Treasury Secretary nominee Scott Bessent urged the Fed to evaluate AI-driven productivity gains, while geopolitical frictions escalated following reports that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps navy seized a U.S. autonomous underwater vehicle in the Strait of Hormuz. The currency also benefits from a +290 basis point overnight carry cushion, with SOFR at 3.88% against foreign peers like TONA at 0.98%. Market attention is geared toward the upcoming U.S. nonfarm payrolls print and rhetoric surrounding prospective renewed diplomatic talks between Washington and Tehran.

JPY.catalyst: The Japanese yen reflects modest weekly gains of +0.08% against the G10 basket, trading on the firm side of its 20-day simple moving average against the dollar at 156.40 while remaining below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. Sentiment has pivoted on hawkish messaging from Bank of Japan board member Hajime Takata, whose remarks on consecutive rate increases pushed the market-implied odds of a 25 basis point hike to 1.25% up to 97%, according to Tokyo Tanshi data. While an overnight carry deficit persists—with TONA at 0.98% against SOFR at 3.88%—the threat of further unwinding of short speculative positions continues to buffer spot declines. Market participants await the publication of the BoJ's July meeting minutes alongside Tokyo-area consumer price data to validate further normalization timelines.
